plan: Store the constructor's dictionary as a deep copy in a single internal tree; to_data() returns a fresh deep copy so callers can never alias internal state.
Provide one in-order recursive walker yielding (item, nesting_level) pairs; drive total_word_count, unresolved_markers, and outline from it so all traversals agree on document order.
Count note words by first replacing each [[?identifier]] marker with a single space, then counting \b\w+\b matches; add each reference's declared word_count.
Collect unresolved identifiers into a set from note-text markers and reference 'unresolved' lists, returning them sorted lexicographically.
Render the outline as the workspace title followed by one line per item: two spaces per nesting level plus 'kind: title'.

Implement move as validate-then-mutate: check string ids, resolve the item, resolve the destination ('workspace' literal or a section/group id), reject non-containers, validate index against the destination's current length, and reject self/descendant containment via an identity check over the moved subtree — all before removing or inserting anything, so any failure leaves to_data() unchanged.
mechanisms: deep-copied single source tree with deep-copy export
shared in-order recursive walker for all queries
marker-stripping regex word count with space substitution
full pre-validation (atomic) move with identity-based descendant cycle check
